topics.label: Opening Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, connects the lecture to the preceding histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Discovery of Proto-Oncogenes and Cellular Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical study of tumor viruses that uncovered cellular proto-oncogenes and describe the laboratory assays used to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Genetic Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer mutations and explain how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative alterations deregulate critical pathways such as the cell cycle.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Genetic Instability and Multi-Step Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the DNA repair, replication, and mitotic defects that cause sequence and chromosomal instability, and how these alterations drive multi-step tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition Syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development across specific syndromes and how these defects behave during tumor progression and treatment.

topics.label: Closing Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the next session.
